English We help people learn English and prove their skills to the world, with qualifications and tests recognised worldwide. International Education The world’s largest provider of international education programmes, qualifications and resources for 3 to 19 year-olds. Cambridge OCR Cambridge OCR is a leading UK awarding body committed to making assessment straightforward, so every student can thrive and achieve the results they deserve. Academic Academic-level research, reference books, higher education textbooks and Bibles published by the Cambridge University Press imprint. Our story From our roots within the University of Cambridge, we have embraced an outward-looking perspective, expanding globally and adopting innovation to meet the evolving needs of learners, teachers, and researchers around the world. Our history informs our present and inspires our future. Learn more Our journey and responsibilities Governance As part of the University of Cambridge, we share a mission ‘to contribute to society through the pursuit of education, learning and research’. Learn more People and planet We inform action around global challenges like climate change through our products and services – ultimately helping to equip a new generation of people able to secure the wellbeing of our planet. Learn more Our global community With 6,380 colleagues in 80 offices around the world, serving over 100 million learners, we value people for who they are, and we are committed to equality, diversity, inclusion and belonging. Learn more Embracing innovation We harness technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) – advancing learning experiences, supporting research and improving our services in our commitment to ethical and impactful innovation. Discover our AI approach Knowledge within reach We believe learning is for everyone. We are committed to making our publications, platforms, and assessments accessible to all, ensuring everyone has opportunity to learn and achieve their potential.             <div>                      <div class="coh-container ssa-component coh-component ssa-component-instance-1e9e8e4a-918c-4733-8724-0b5ce12404f6 coh-component-instance-1e9e8e4a-918c-4733-8724-0b5ce12404f6 ssa-instance-a5ecdfe6e4949a6690004bdac7e35497 coh-ce-cpt_main_page_content-af188e5d" >  <div class="coh-container  semi-sanctioned-     ssa-instance-a5ecdfe6e4949a6690004bdac7e35497 coh-ce-cpt_main_page_content-718c2162" >  <div class="coh-wysiwyg ssa-instance-a5ecdfe6e4949a6690004bdac7e35497 coh-ce-cpt_main_page_content-a04f99c3"  >    <p class="text-align-center"><span><strong>At the end of July, the first ever cohort of students graduated with a G12++ certificate in Shatila refugee camp in Beirut. The G12++, developed by Alsama Project, with support from Cambridge University Press & Assessment, is a high school equivalent qualification designed for young people forcibly displaced from their homes.</strong></span></p><p class="text-align-center"> </p><img data-entity-uuid="e1bce9ae-d4ad-4b7d-ae80-cba05cfaa8e7" data-entity-type="file" src="https://drupal-s3fs-prod.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/inline-images/dsc_0332-3265x1837_2.jpg" width="3265" height="1837" alt="Graduates celebrating on stage as confetti falls" class="align-center" loading="lazy"><p><a href="https://alsamaproject.com/who-we-are">Alsama Project</a>, an award-winning educational NGO based in Lebanon, established the G12++ as a global solution for young people excluded from formal education systems.</p><p>Of 49 million young people worldwide displaced by crises such as conflict, violence and persecution, only 9 percent attend university, compared to the 42 percent global average. <span>The G12++ certificate addresses this systemic gap as the world’s first qualification designed for displaced youth.</span> It is an internationally benchmarked and digitally scalable qualification.</p><p><span>For students, it provides a recognised pathway to further education and skilled employment. For universities, it provides a credible admissions tool that unlocks the potential of an untapped pool of talent.</span></p><p>Over the past two years, Cambridge has worked with Alsama to strengthen the assessment approach and support exam development of G12++, drawing on experience delivering assessments to more than eight million learners each year in over 170 countries.</p> </div> </div> </div> 
                         <div class="coh-container ssa-component coh-component ssa-component-instance-598d472a-1f21-4862-a6e8-a99456b12165 coh-component-instance-598d472a-1f21-4862-a6e8-a99456b12165 coh-video-width--     coh-ce-cpt_video-5c730196 coh-container-boxed" >  <div class="coh-container ssa-instance-3b5add6fdf7f25bba5e8243d439c0f11 coh-ce-cpt_video-71920144" >   




	<h3 class="coh-heading coh-video-heading"></h3>
	<p class="coh-paragraph coh-video-paragraph"></p>
	
<div class="media--remote-video media--image-with-caption">
  
  <div class="video-container" style="">
        <div class="lite-video-wrapper">
            <lite-youtube videoid="dHqJRxsDBes"></lite-youtube>
          </div>

 </div> </div>    
                 <div class="coh-container ssa-component coh-component ssa-component-instance-ec42a920-1dbd-4c11-80a4-73da78c2f407 coh-component-instance-ec42a920-1dbd-4c11-80a4-73da78c2f407 ssa-instance-b42cd6837269437adc86d416be99db1b coh-ce-cpt_main_page_content-af188e5d" >  <div class="coh-container  semi-sanctioned-     ssa-instance-b42cd6837269437adc86d416be99db1b coh-ce-cpt_main_page_content-718c2162" >  <div class="coh-wysiwyg ssa-instance-b42cd6837269437adc86d416be99db1b coh-ce-cpt_main_page_content-a04f99c3"  >    <p>This first cohort of G12++ test-takers is exceptional. Many were completely illiterate when they joined Alsama Project just six years ago. Now they have won full scholarships to study at universities around the world, including in the UK, Canada, India, Lebanon, and remotely through programmes such as the <a href="https://www.pace.cam.ac.uk/">University of Cambridge's Professional and Continuing Education</a> (PACE).</p><p>Star Alsama student, Fatima, earned the G12++’s top mark in 2026. In September 2026, she will study Environmental Science at the University of Leicester – one of the six partner universities that accept the G12++ as an admissions tool. Other partner universities include the University of Cambridge, Kent University, Arizona State University, Moravian University and MUBS, Beirut.</p><p> </p><p> </p><figure role="group" class="align-right">
<img alt="Fatima scored top marks in the first cohort of students achieving the G12++" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-uuid="dda63387-f80f-4382-9a0b-45af2672e7e0" height="383" src="https://drupal-s3fs-prod.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/inline-images/Enlarged%20Media%20library_0.png" width="255" loading="lazy">
<figcaption>Fatima scored top marks in the first cohort of students achieving the G12++</figcaption>
</figure>
<p> </p><p> </p><blockquote><p><em>"The G12++ changed the direction of my life. Alsama gave me education, and the G12++ gave me the chance to prove that education. Because of the G12++. I am going to university."</em></p><p><span class="coh-color-cambridge-dark-blue"><strong>Star Alsama student, Fatima J</strong></span></p></blockquote><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><img src="https://drupal-s3fs-prod.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/inline-images/Jane%20Mann_0.jpg" data-entity-uuid="1c336397-1d59-454e-bc0a-85823519bfc4" data-entity-type="file" alt="A portrait of Jane Mann, Cambridge's Chief Education Officer" width="368" height="345" class="align-left" loading="lazy"><blockquote><p><em>"I'm so excited to see the first students graduate with the G12++ qualification, which is a significant milestone not only for them personally but for education for displaced students more widely. The G12++ was created to provide a credible pathway for learners whose education has been interrupted by conflict and displacement, and these graduates are proof of what can be achieved when talent is given the opportunity to flourish.</em></p><p><em>"We congratulate every student on their achievement and look forward to working with the Alsama Project and partners around the world to help many more displaced young people access higher education, training and employment."</em></p><p><cite><span class="coh-color-cambridge-dark-blue">Jane Mann, Cambridge's Chief Education Officer</span></cite></p></blockquote><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><p> </p><figure role="group" class="align-center">
<img alt="Alsama's Meike Ziervogel, centre, at the G12++ graduation celebrations" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-uuid="d3ff93b7-077e-4efc-b353-fffd8b66bd2b" height="3264" src="https://drupal-s3fs-prod.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/inline-images/DSC_0307.jpeg" width="4928" loading="lazy">
<figcaption>Alsama's Meike Ziervogel, centre, at the G12++ graduation celebrations</figcaption>
</figure>
<p> </p><p><strong>Alsama Chief Executive Officer and co-founder Meike Ziervogel told students:</strong></p><blockquote><p><em><span>"Back in January 2020, many of you could not look me in the eyes, didn't know what you wanted from life, couldn't even write your own names. Now you are ready to go to university, to get a job. By being the inspiration for Alsama, you changed the lives of many young people."</span></em></p><p><cite><em><span class="coh-color-cambridge-dark-blue">Meike Ziervogel, Chief Executive Officer and Alsama Co-Founder</span></em></cite></p></blockquote> </div> </div> </div> 
                                     <div class="coh-container ssa-component coh-component ssa-component-instance-0f991e60-4336-40ed-8567-b472ce98c783 coh-component-instance-0f991e60-4336-40ed-8567-b472ce98c783 in-page-banner--black in-page-banner--padding-bottom-   color-override__none  ssa-instance-69ce366ba3f425c9d6e99ab7a935eee1 coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-6440fd09" > <h6 class="coh-heading coh-style-value-sans-heading coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-d2f5a66a"  >  </h6>  <div class="coh-container coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-4fbcf56f" >    <p class="coh-paragraph coh-style-body-regular coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-3c9cc834"  >Cambridge and Alsama are looking to engage with fundraisers, universities, employers, TVET institutions, policymakers and other partners to support them as they scale the qualification worldwide.<br />
</p>    </div>      <div class="coh-container coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-fc65d442" >    <a href="https://www.cambridge.org/about-us/education-everywhere" class="coh-link coh-style-dark-button coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-3f7f96fd" target="_blank" > Read how Cambridge supports Education Everywhere    </a>     <a href="https://www.cambridge.org/gb/partnership/news-and-events/news/cambridge-and-alsama-project-partner-on-new-schoolleaver-qualification-to-help-refugees-and-displaced-youth-access-university-training-and-jobs-worldwide" class="coh-link coh-style-dark-button coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-1da41fa5" target="_blank" > Read more about the new G12++ qualification    </a>     <a href="https://www.cambridge.org/gb/partnership/news-and-events/cambridge-supports-ngo-alsama-to-develop-schoolleaver-exam-for-refugees" class="coh-link coh-style-dark-button coh-ce-cpt_in_page_banner-1da41fa5" target="_blank" > Find out more on Alsama and Cambridge partnership    </a>  </div>      </div>

Remove item Keep Breadcrumb Home News and insights First students graduate with Alsama's G12++ qualification News and Events Open share menu Share Close share menu Facebook X LinkedIn Copy link First students graduate with Alsama's G12++ qualification At the end of July, the first ever cohort of students graduated with a G12++ certificate in Shatila refugee camp in Beirut. 12 Aug 2026 Matt Midgley Community Future of education Learning At the end of July, the first ever cohort of students graduated with a G12++ certificate in Shatila refugee camp in Beirut. The G12++, developed by Alsama Project, with support from Cambridge University Press & Assessment, is a high school equivalent qualification designed for young people forcibly displaced from their homes.   Alsama Project , an award-winning educational NGO based in Lebanon, established the G12++ as a global solution for young people excluded from formal education systems. Of 49 million young people worldwide displaced by crises such as conflict, violence and persecution, only 9 percent attend university, compared to the 42 percent global average. The G12++ certificate addresses this systemic gap as the world’s first qualification designed for displaced youth. It is an internationally benchmarked and digitally scalable qualification. For students, it provides a recognised pathway to further education and skilled employment. For universities, it provides a credible admissions tool that unlocks the potential of an untapped pool of talent. Over the past two years, Cambridge has worked with Alsama to strengthen the assessment approach and support exam development of G12++, drawing on experience delivering assessments to more than eight million learners each year in over 170 countries. This first cohort of G12++ test-takers is exceptional. Many were completely illiterate when they joined Alsama Project just six years ago. Now they have won full scholarships to study at universities around the world, including in the UK, Canada, India, Lebanon, and remotely through programmes such as the University of Cambridge's Professional and Continuing Education (PACE). Star Alsama student, Fatima, earned the G12++’s top mark in 2026. In September 2026, she will study Environmental Science at the University of Leicester – one of the six partner universities that accept the G12++ as an admissions tool. Other partner universities include the University of Cambridge, Kent University, Arizona State University, Moravian University and MUBS, Beirut.     Fatima scored top marks in the first cohort of students achieving the G12++     "The G12++ changed the direction of my life. Alsama gave me education, and the G12++ gave me the chance to prove that education. Because of the G12++. I am going to university." Star Alsama student, Fatima J                 "I'm so excited to see the first students graduate with the G12++ qualification, which is a significant milestone not only for them personally but for education for displaced students more widely. The G12++ was created to provide a credible pathway for learners whose education has been interrupted by conflict and displacement, and these graduates are proof of what can be achieved when talent is given the opportunity to flourish. "We congratulate every student on their achievement and look forward to working with the Alsama Project and partners around the world to help many more displaced young people access higher education, training and employment." Jane Mann, Cambridge's Chief Education Officer         Alsama's Meike Ziervogel, centre, at the G12++ graduation celebrations   Alsama Chief Executive Officer and co-founder Meike Ziervogel told students: "Back in January 2020, many of you could not look me in the eyes, didn't know what you wanted from life, couldn't even write your own names. Now you are ready to go to university, to get a job. By being the inspiration for Alsama, you changed the lives of many young people." Meike Ziervogel, Chief Executive Officer and Alsama Co-Founder Cambridge and Alsama are looking to engage with fundraisers, universities, employers, TVET institutions, policymakers and other partners to support them as they scale the qualification worldwide.
